source_claims.statement: Gathered context from JavaScript without source code. Focused on avatar generation and download endpoints.
Standard path traversal, encodings, null bytes on download endpoint produced only Internal Server Errors. Abandoned that fixation; examined other JS (main.js) and found SSRF allowing file://.

research_questions.formulation: After standard traversal techniques fail on the obvious download endpoint, do other JavaScript-referenced endpoints expose a different file-access primitive?
research_questions.anchor: pivot from download endpoint to other JS files
research_questions.uncertainty_reduced: whether file access is limited to the download path
research_questions.assumption_challenged: that the download endpoint is the only relevant surface

environment_model_updates: Download endpoint rejects standard traversal with errors
main.js contains an SSRF that accepts file:// and returns file content

systematic_vs_exploratory.systematic: testing standard path traversal variants on the download endpoint
systematic_vs_exploratory.exploratory: examining additional JS files after the primary endpoint failed

negative_inconclusive: All standard traversal techniques on download endpoint produced errors (bounded negative on that endpoint)
forbidden_inferences: Do not treat download endpoint failures as proof no LFI exists
The successful SSRF was found by looking beyond the initial hint
next_evidence_actions: Note bug bounty reporting and quick fix
layer_b_candidate_principles: When an obvious endpoint rejects standard techniques with errors, examine other client-side references for alternative entry points before stopping
JavaScript can reveal SSRF or proxy endpoints that accept file:// even when direct download paths do not
model_vs_harness: Deciding to abandon the download endpoint and look at other JS is model judgment; systematic testing of traversal variants can be harness.
